reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a robust, piecewise-constant (staircase) waveform with a fundamental period of ~98 points, as confirmed by the reference_cycle_plan and estimated_period. Each cycle consists of three phases: a rapid descent (~20–25 points) from a high plateau (~+0.5 to +0.75) to a low trough (~−1.25), a flat or slightly rising bottom segment (~30–40 points) near −1.25, and a gradual ascent (~35–45 points) back to the high plateau. The amplitude (peak-to-trough) is consistently ~1.75–2.0 in robust-standardized units, matching the catalog’s amplitude_90 (~2.0–2.2). Peaks are broad, flat-topped plateaus; troughs are similarly flat but occasionally show minor jaggedness (e.g., candidate 2 at ~1813, candidate 3 at ~2669), likely due to quantization or minor noise. Trends per point are near-zero (|slope| < 0.0018), confirming stationarity after robust standardization; curvature is negligible except for a slight positive curvature in candidate 2 (catalog curvature=0.048), which appears visually as a subtly rounded ascent—still within acceptable variation. Noise is minimal: values are quantized to a coarse grid (steps of ~0.25), indicating discretization rather than Gaussian noise; no high-frequency jitter is present. Boundary truncation is not an issue—the candidates are cleanly cut at cycle boundaries (e.g., candidate 0 ends at peak, candidate 1 starts at peak), preserving full-cycle morphology. Acceptable variation includes minor differences in plateau width, exact trough depth (−1.20 to −1.30), and occasional single-point spikes (<0.25 deviation) during transitions.

reference_profiles.description: Single-cycle (1P) staircase: begins at high plateau (~+0.75), descends sharply to −1.25 over ~25 points, holds flat near trough for ~30 points, then rises gradually over ~40 points back to plateau. Clean, symmetric transition shapes; no jaggedness or outliers. Visually the most ‘ideal’ cycle.

Three-cycle (3P) excerpt showing identical repeating morphology: sharp descent, flat trough, gradual rise. Minor step irregularities in ascent (e.g., small overshoots at ~984, 1076) but overall highly consistent. No anomalies; matches candidate 0 cycle-for-cycle when aligned.

Three-cycle (3P) excerpt with same core morphology but slightly rounded ascent (visible curvature) and one minor double-dip trough at ~1813–1815. Plateau heights vary slightly (+0.5 to +0.65); trough depth is consistent (−1.25). The curvature is subtle and likely benign—within catalog’s low roughness/curvature bounds.

Five-cycle (5P) excerpt; strongest evidence of normality due to longest span. All cycles replicate the staircase pattern faithfully. One minor spike at ~2669 (brief +0.25 excursion during ascent) and another at ~2849, but both are transient and within ±0.25 of baseline—likely quantization artifacts. Amplitude and timing remain stable across all five cycles.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer candidate 0 for single-cycle query matching (best signal-to-noise, ideal morphology). Use candidate 1 or 3 for multi-cycle queries: candidate 1 for 3-cycle windows (cleaner transitions), candidate 3 for ≥4-cycle windows (more statistical confidence). Candidate 2 is acceptable but use only when curvature or minor trough variation is observed in the query—its slight deviations are normal, not anomalous. Never discard a candidate solely for minor quantization spikes (<0.3 MAD); treat them as part of the expected discrete noise profile.
uncertainties: Exact quantization step size (grid spacing) is inferred (~0.25) but not precisely measurable from plots alone
